subject: encode-cpu: additive bridge hunk n2mb_wait_seq (own function, after n2mb_wait_pending) - adding now
body:
For cross-command pipelining (opt-in TEGU_ASYNC_PIPELINE=1, default OFF) the finish thread must wait for ITS command (jobs <= seq) without holding the bridge lock, so the execute thread can keep submitting the next command. New function only, nothing else changed in your regions:
int n2mb_wait_seq(uintptr_t,uint64_t seq,uint64_t *failed_job): under lock: if broken -> NOTREADY; if async!=1 or !pending or seq==0 -> 0 (nothing queued at or before seq that is not already reaped... see note); clamp seq to pending; unlock; kernel WAIT_SEQ{seq,5000} OUTSIDE the lock (2 timeout retries like wait_pending); relock: failure -> broken=1, async_failed=out[2]; success -> if pending<=seq pending=0 (nothing newer was submitted meanwhile). Header: declaration + comment next to n2mb_wait_pending. Concurrency assumption to verify on device: the kernel user client accepts SUBMIT_JM/WAIT_SEQ from two threads of one client concurrently (0090 drops the gpu lock around delays); if not, pipelining only loses its overlap, never correctness. Tell me if you object.
